name: Universal Credit
administrator: Department for Work and Pensions / Department for Communities (NI)
summary: A means-tested payment for people on a low income, out of work, or unable to work. Savings and household circumstances matter.
documents: National Insurance number for the official claim
next_steps: Use an independent benefits calculator for a fuller estimate.
Check the official Universal Credit eligibility page for your nation.
If eligible, apply through the official government service and report household changes promptly.
notes: This app uses a simplified screen. Official rules include work allowances, earnings tapers, housing elements, capital rules and immigration/residency tests.

name: Council Tax Reduction / Council Tax Support
summary: A local reduction in Council Tax for some low-income households and people receiving benefits.
next_steps: Find your local council using your postcode.
Review the council's own Council Tax Reduction rules.
Apply directly to the council and ask whether backdating is available.
notes: Each council runs its own scheme, so the exact reduction and rules vary by area.

name: Rate Rebate / Housing Benefit and Rate Relief (Northern Ireland)
administrator: Northern Ireland Housing Executive / Land & Property Services
summary: Northern Ireland uses domestic rates rather than Council Tax. Rate Rebate or Housing Benefit/Rate Relief may help eligible households.
next_steps: Check whether Rate Rebate or pension-age Housing Benefit/Rate Relief fits your circumstances.
Use nidirect and the Housing Executive for the correct route.
Apply through the official NI service.
notes: Working-age households on Universal Credit generally use Rate Rebate for help with rates.

name: Child Benefit
summary: A payment for a person responsible for a qualifying child, normally under 16 or under 20 in approved education or training.
documents: Bank details for the official claim
Education/training information for older qualifying children
next_steps: Check which person should make the claim if two adults are responsible for the same child.
Review eligibility for children aged 16 to 19 in approved education or training.
Claim through HMRC's official service.
notes: Higher-income households may face the High Income Child Benefit Charge; that is separate from basic eligibility.

name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
summary: Extra-cost support for eligible people with a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability that affects daily living or mobility.
documents: Examples of how the condition affects daily activities
next_steps: Check whether your condition affects daily-living or mobility activities.
Gather specific real-life examples and supporting information.
Start the official claim for your nation.
notes: PIP is not means-tested. Scotland uses Adult Disability Payment instead.

name: Adult Disability Payment (Scotland)
summary: Scotland's disability benefit for eligible people aged 16 to State Pension age whose disability or long-term condition affects everyday life.
documents: Supporting information from a professional or wider support network
Examples of daily-living or mobility impact
next_steps: Use the Social Security Scotland eligibility checker.
Gather supporting information about how your condition affects you.
Apply online or by phone/paper through mygov.scot.
notes: Income and savings are not taken into account for Adult Disability Payment.

name: Attendance Allowance
summary: Support for people at or above State Pension age who need help with personal care or supervision because of disability or a health condition.
documents: Examples of help needed day and night
next_steps: Check that you have reached State Pension age.
Describe care and supervision needs in detail, including difficult days.
Apply through the official service for your nation.
notes: Scotland uses Pension Age Disability Payment instead.

name: Pension Age Disability Payment (Scotland)
summary: Scotland's disability support for eligible people of State Pension age with care or supervision needs.
next_steps: Use the mygov.scot eligibility checker.
Collect supporting information that confirms your condition or needs.
Apply through Social Security Scotland.
notes: Rules differ for people in care homes and for applications linked to terminal illness.

name: Carer's Allowance
summary: Support for some people who provide at least 35 hours of care each week for a person receiving a qualifying disability benefit.
documents: Details of the person you care for
National Insurance number for the official claim
next_steps: Confirm the person you care for receives a qualifying disability benefit.
Check the 35-hour caring requirement and current earnings rules.
Review how a claim could affect both people's other benefits before submitting.
notes: Scotland has replaced Carer's Allowance with Carer Support Payment.

name: Carer Support Payment (Scotland)
summary: Scotland's main benefit for eligible unpaid carers. It replaced Carer's Allowance in Scotland.
documents: Details of the qualifying disability benefit received by the person you care for
next_steps: Confirm you provide at least 35 hours of qualifying care a week.
Check current earnings and residence rules.
Apply through Social Security Scotland.
notes: From 2026, Scotland also has Scottish Carer Supplement and Carer Additional Person Payment components in the wider carer-support system.

name: New Style Jobseeker's Allowance (JSA)
summary: A contribution-based unemployment benefit for some people with sufficient recent Class 1 National Insurance contributions.
documents: Bank details for the official claim
next_steps: Check your recent National Insurance contribution record.
Confirm you are under State Pension age and meet work-hour conditions.
Apply through the official service for your nation.
notes: Savings and a partner's savings do not normally affect New Style JSA.

name: New Style Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
summary: A contribution-based benefit for some people under State Pension age whose health condition or disability limits how much they can work.
next_steps: Check your recent National Insurance contributions or credits.
Get a fit note if the official claim requires one.
Apply through the correct government service for your nation.
notes: You cannot normally receive New Style ESA at the same time as New Style JSA or Statutory Sick Pay.

name: Pension Credit
summary: An income-related benefit for eligible people who have reached State Pension age; it can also open access to other support.
next_steps: Confirm you have reached State Pension age.
Use the Pension Credit calculator or a benefits adviser.
Apply through the Pension Service or the NI equivalent.
notes: Savings do not create a simple hard cut-off, but assumed income from capital can affect the award.

name: Tax-Free Childcare
summary: Government top-ups toward approved childcare for eligible working families with qualifying children.
documents: National Insurance numbers for the official service
next_steps: Check your child's age and both adults' work/income conditions if you have a partner.
Compare Tax-Free Childcare with Universal Credit childcare support before switching.
Apply through the Childcare Service.
notes: A person with expected adjusted net income over £100,000 cannot normally qualify.

name: Healthy Start
summary: Help to buy healthy food and milk, plus vitamins, for some pregnant people and families with children under 4.
next_steps: Check the pregnancy/child-age condition.
Check whether you receive a qualifying benefit or meet an exception.
Apply using the NHS Healthy Start service.
notes: Scotland uses Best Start Foods instead.

name: Best Start Foods (Scotland)
summary: Scottish support that can help eligible pregnant people and families with young children buy healthy food and milk.
next_steps: Check the current Best Start Foods age and income/benefit rules.
See whether a combined Best Start Grant application is relevant.
Apply through Social Security Scotland.
notes: Eligibility and payment rules are set by Social Security Scotland.

name: Warm Home Discount
administrator: Department for Energy Security & Net Zero / participating suppliers
summary: A one-off electricity-bill discount for eligible households. Eligibility routes differ across England/Wales and Scotland.
next_steps: Check the current scheme-year rules for your nation.
Confirm your electricity supplier participates.
Follow any letter or supplier instructions if data matching cannot confirm eligibility automatically.
notes: The 2026/27 scheme is £150; Northern Ireland uses different energy-support schemes.

name: Cold Weather Payment / Winter Heating Payment
administrator: DWP / Social Security Scotland / Department for Communities (NI)
summary: Automatic winter support for some households receiving qualifying benefits. Scotland uses Winter Heating Payment rather than Cold Weather Payment.
documents: Usually no separate application; keep benefit and address details current
next_steps: Check whether you receive a qualifying benefit.
Make sure the relevant agency has accurate household information, especially about young children.
Use the official scheme page for your nation.
notes: Cold Weather Payment depends on qualifying cold periods; Scotland's Winter Heating Payment does not depend on local temperature.

name: Winter Fuel Payment / Scottish pension-age winter support
summary: Winter heating support for many people of qualifying age. Scotland has a separate pension-age winter-heating payment system.
documents: Benefit or State Pension information if relevant
next_steps: Check the qualifying birth-date and residence rules for the current winter.
Check whether payment should be automatic or whether you need to claim.
If in Scotland, use the current Social Security Scotland pension-age winter-heating guidance.
notes: For winter 2026/27, Winter Fuel Payment in England, Wales and NI is subject to current age/residence rules and recovery through tax above the published income threshold.

name: NHS Low Income Scheme
summary: Help with certain NHS health costs for eligible people on a low income who are not already fully exempt through another route.
next_steps: Check whether you already receive full help through a qualifying benefit or exemption.
Check the current capital limits and what costs can be covered.
Apply online if eligible or use an HC1 form.
notes: Northern Ireland has different health-cost arrangements. Scotland already provides some services such as prescriptions without charge.

name: Support for Mortgage Interest (SMI)
summary: A repayable loan that can help eligible homeowners receiving a qualifying benefit with mortgage or qualifying home-improvement loan interest.
next_steps: Confirm you receive a qualifying benefit and meet any waiting period.
Review the loan terms and repayment implications carefully.
Complete the official form with your lender if you choose to accept an offer.
notes: SMI is a loan, not a grant, and must normally be repaid with interest when the home is sold or transferred.

name: Maternity Allowance
summary: A payment for some people taking time off to have a baby who cannot get Statutory Maternity Pay, including some self-employed people.
documents: SMP1 form if your employer says you do not qualify for Statutory Maternity Pay
next_steps: First check Statutory Maternity Pay eligibility if you are an employee.
If SMP is not available, check Maternity Allowance work/earnings conditions.
Apply from the permitted point in pregnancy through the official service.
notes: Maternity Allowance can affect some other benefits.

name: Free School Meals / devolved school-meal support
summary: School-meal support varies by UK nation, age and benefit status. England expanded benefits-based eligibility for 2026/27.
next_steps: Check your nation/local authority rules and your child's school year.
Ask the school or council how eligibility is verified.
Apply or confirm entitlement through the local process.
notes: This app only flags school-meal support as worth checking; nation-specific rules must be confirmed locally.

name: Free debt advice and financial guidance
summary: Free, confidential debt advice can help prioritise arrears, negotiate with creditors and check benefit entitlements.
documents: Arrears/court or enforcement letters if any
next_steps: Use MoneyHelper's debt-advice locator to find free help.
Prioritise housing, energy, council-tax/rates and court-related debts before unsecured credit.
Avoid firms that demand large upfront fees or guarantee debt write-offs.
notes: This is not a government benefit. It is included because debt, loans and credit stress are part of the app's financial-needs assessment.

name: Independent UK benefits calculator / adviser check
administrator: Independent calculators listed by GOV.UK / local advisers
summary: GOV.UK lists free independent calculators such as entitledto, Turn2us and Policy in Practice for more detailed benefits estimates.
next_steps: Run one of the calculators listed by GOV.UK.
Use accurate figures from recent documents.
For complex cases, speak to a local benefits adviser rather than relying only on an automated result.
notes: Some calculators are not accurate for certain groups such as some students, prisoners, people in residential care, or people with complex immigration status.
